newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel barges jump $3 on short covering.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel barges jump $3 on short covering.

text.p: European fuel barges jumped on Thursday as big players bought to cover short positions, while low sulphur markets were steady and quiet, traders said.
High sulphur barge deals were heard done at $86 and $87 fob a tonne, $2-$3 above yesterday. Healthy bunker demand was also reported tightening the ARA market.

"There is nothing in storage and it all has to come from refiners and they are not producing much," said one trader. "We need Russian cargoes to cover the shorts and nothing is coming in at the moment."
One percent cracked markets were illiquid, with paper business very quiet and prices roughly steady, despite the downward pressure imposed by falling crude futures.
The rise in barge prices prevented one percent from slumping below $92/$93 a tonne, one trader suggested.
Low sulphur straight-run was also weak, with a 30kt cargo heard traded late on Wednesday into a British refinery at $104 fob, at the top end of the current price range.
Another promptish parcel from Scandinavia was under active discussion, dealers said.
